cohort: 26,091 nulliparous women with singleton gestations between 24-43 weeks from Washington State birth certificate data linked to hospital records from 1987 through 2009
finding: Young adolescents (aged 11-14 years) had a decreased risk of cesarean and operative vaginal delivery compared to young adults (aged 20-24 years), but their neonates faced higher risks of preterm delivery, low birthweight, very low birthweight, and death.
birth_weight: Young adolescents had an increased risk of low and very low birthweight compared to young adults.
